title: New tiny jellyfish species Copula lucentia discovered off Alicante, Spain
content:
Scientists have identified a new jellyfish species, Copula lucentia, in the Mediterranean Sea. The tiny medusa, measuring only a few millimeters, was found off the coast of El Campello in Alicante.

The species was formally described in 2024 by a research team from the University of Alicante’s Marine Laboratory in Dénia. The laboratory is part of the university’s Ramón Margalef Multidisciplinary Institute for Environmental Research.
summary: Copula lucentia is a tiny jellyfish measuring just a few millimeters, discovered off El Campello in Alicante, Spain. It was formally described in 2024 by a research team at the University of Alicante Marine Laboratory in Dénia, part of the university's Ramón Margalef Multidisciplinary Institute for Environmental Research.
author: Phys.org

title: Kyushu University researchers find H3mm15 histone variant essential for mouse sperm development
content:
Kyushu University researchers discovered H3mm15, a histone H3.3 subvariant, is essential for normal sperm development in mice by regulating gene expression during spermatogenesis.  

The study shows H3mm15 cannot replace conventional H3.3; despite only three amino acid differences, the two proteins behave differently within chromatin, the DNA‑protein structure that packages genetic material.
summary: Kyushu University researchers find H3mm15 histone variant essential for mouse sperm development.
author: Phys.org

title: University of Tokyo researchers find hidden earthquake traces in Kumano Sea sediment
content:
Researchers at the University of Tokyo have applied a new type of radiocarbon analysis to a sediment core taken from the Kumano Sea off Japan’s coast. The study, published in the journal Radiocarbon, uncovered multiple “hidden” traces of previously unknown earthquakes in the Nankai Trough.

The findings add detail to the seismic history of the region, where a future megaquake is anticipated. By reconstructing a more accurate picture of past seismic activity, the research aims to improve predictions of future geophysical events and aid in disaster preparedness.
summary: Researchers at the University of Tokyo have used a new type of radiocarbon analysis to study a sediment core taken from the Kumano Sea off the coast of Japan. This has revealed multiple "hidden" traces of previously unknown earthquakes in the Nankai Trough, where the country's next megaquake is expected to occur.
author: Phys.org

title: New simulation model enhances nursing staff empowerment and autonomy
content: A new clinical simulation model has been introduced to strengthen the empowerment and autonomy of nursing staff. Unlike traditional methods that mainly assess technical skills and compliance with medical standards from a generic, interprofessional view, this model emphasizes nursing‑specific aspects such as care ethics, relational presence with patients, and emotional management among nurses.
summary: A new clinical simulation model strengthens the empowerment and autonomy of nursing staff. Previous simulation methods mainly assessed technical skills and compliance, overlooking care ethics, relational presence, and emotional management.
author: Phys.org

title: Dead star's double ring of planetary wreckage offers preview of Sun's future
content:
Astronomers have discovered a strange double ring of planetary wreckage around a dead star, offering a possible preview of what might happen to our Solar System in the distant future.

The two rings are separated by a mysterious gap that researchers believe is maintained by surviving planetary bodies, including one potentially as large as Pluto or the Moon.

Their different chemical compositions suggest they may contain the remains of separate destroyed planets.
summary: Astronomers discovered a strange double ring of planetary wreckage around a dead star. The rings are separated by a gap maintained by surviving bodies, possibly as large as Pluto or the Moon, and their different chemical compositions suggest they contain remains of destroyed planets.
author: Science Daily

title: Rubin Observatory discovers two hidden companions of the Milky Way. Hundreds more may be waiting
content:
The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has identified two previously unknown companions of the Milky Way from preliminary observations that cover only 7 % of the night sky.  

The discoveries include an extremely faint galaxy located 355,000 light‑years away and a star cluster concealed behind cosmic dust.  

Scientists believe that hundreds of additional satellite galaxies may still be hidden, and the Observatory’s powerful telescope could eventually reveal them.
summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has already uncovered two previously unknown companions of the Milky Way using preliminary observations covering just 7% of the night sky.
author: Science Daily

title: UC San Francisco scientists develop brain‑specific therapy that eliminates tumors in mice
content: UC San Francisco scientists developed a new cancer therapy that stays inactive until it reaches the brain, where it activates to attack tumors. The therapy uses engineered immune cells called B‑SYNC CAR‑T cells. In two mouse models, the B‑SYNC CAR‑T cells completely eliminated diffuse midline glioma (DMG), an aggressive childhood brain cancer that is almost always fatal within a year.
summary: UC San Francisco scientists created B‑SYNC CAR‑T cells that activate only in the brain to target tumors. In two mouse models, the therapy completely eliminated diffuse midline glioma, a fatal childhood brain cancer.
author: Science Daily

title: Einstein's Equations Reveal Gravitational Reconnection That Releases Energy
content:
Scientists have identified a new phenomenon hidden in Einstein’s equations. Researchers at Columbia University and Universidad Adolfo Ibáñez describe a theoretical process called gravitational reconnection.

In this process, structures within gravitational fields can break apart and then reconnect, transferring energy into matter. The discovery suggests gravity can release energy through such reconnections, a behavior not previously highlighted in Einstein’s framework.
summary: Researchers at Columbia University and Universidad Adolfo Ibáñez identified a theoretical process called gravitational reconnection, in which structures within gravitational fields can break apart and reconnect, transferring energy into matter. The process transfers energy into matter.
author: Science Daily

title: New Amazon fish species Laimosemion laranja discovered, already endangered
content:
Researchers discovered a new species of tiny orange‑patterned fish in the Brazilian Amazon. The killifish, named Laimosemion laranja, measures less than three centimeters and was found in only three small forest pools.  

Its limited habitat faces threats from mining, deforestation, pollution, and expanding development.
summary: Researchers discovered a tiny orange-patterned fish, Laimosemion laranja, in the Brazilian Amazon. The species, less than three centimeters long and found only in three small forest pools, faces habitat threats from mining, deforestation, pollution, and expanding development.
author: Science Daily

title: Sticky marine snow can move over six times more carbon to the deep ocean
content: Scientists have found that the stickiness of underwater “marine snow” significantly affects how much carbon sinks to the deep ocean. Because gooier particles are less readily broken down by bacteria, they can carry more than six times the carbon to depth, highlighting an unexpected link between ocean slime and the planet’s climate.
summary: Scientists have discovered that the stickiness of underwater “marine snow” plays an important role in how much carbon reaches the deep ocean. Gooier particles resist bacterial breakdown and can transport more than six times as much carbon to the depths, revealing an unexpected link between ocean slime and Earth's climate.
author: Science Daily

title: Colombian fossil discovery reveals "Biotic Inflection" in ancient ocean
content: A remarkable fossil discovery in Colombia is challenging how scientists understand major evolutionary changes in Earth's history. Researchers uncovered an incredibly diverse ancient marine ecosystem where giant reptiles, sharks, and other creatures thrived as older evolutionary groups approached extinction and newer ones emerged. They call this previously unrecognized pattern a "Biotic Inflection," suggesting that major transformations in life can occur without mass extinctions.
summary: Scientists discovered a diverse ancient marine ecosystem in Colombia where giant reptiles, sharks, and other creatures thrived as older evolutionary groups approached extinction and newer ones emerged. They named this previously unrecognized pattern the "Biotic Inflection," indicating that major evolutionary transformations can occur without mass extinctions.
author: Science Daily

title: Protein Miro1 buildup linked to insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes
content: Scientists have identified a protein called Miro1 as a potential driver of insulin resistance in Type 2 diabetes. Preclinical experiments demonstrated that removing this protein restores muscle response to insulin. Additionally, research found that exercise lowers Miro1 levels in people with diabetes, suggesting a new pathway for treating the disease.
summary: Scientists found that a buildup of the protein Miro1 may drive insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes, with preclinical experiments showing that removing it restores muscle response to insulin. Exercise was also found to lower Miro1 levels in people with diabetes, revealing a potential new treatment pathway.
author: Science Daily

title: Jensen Huang Sends Memo to Nvidia Employees Acknowledging Affair
content:
Jensen Huang, chief executive officer of Nvidia Corp., appeared at a media briefing in Tokyo on Thursday, July 16 2026, following the company’s “Japan AI Ecosystem” reception. The event highlighted Nvidia’s ongoing engagement with Japan’s technology community.

Japan announced plans to purchase 27,500 next‑generation Rubin chips from Nvidia to support the development of a domestic foundational AI model for robots. The purchase is part of Japan’s broader strategy to build homegrown AI capabilities.

On Sunday, Nvidia disclosed that it had begun an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, an AI executive and agent of the Chinese government. The Board of Directors announced the investigation, and Huang sent a memo to Nvidia employees acknowledging the affair. The memo began: “To my colleagues at NVIDIA, I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang sent a memo to employees apologizing for being unfaithful to his wife. The company announced it is investigating his relationship with Alice Huang, an AI executive and Chinese government agent.
author: The Verge

title: US offers $20 million reward and possible relocation for info on Iran’s nuclear program
content: The U.S. State Department announced a $20 million reward and potential relocation assistance for information regarding Iran’s nuclear program. The announcement cited the regime’s failure to comply with IAEA safeguards obligations, which the department stated resulted in the agency losing "continuity of knowledge."
summary: The State Department announced a $20 million reward and possible relocation for information on Iran’s nuclear program. It also said the regime’s lack of compliance with IAEA safeguards has caused the agency to lose continuity of knowledge.
author: Euronews

title: US launches new targeted strikes on Iran as Trump claims progress in talks with Tehran
content: The US military carried out new airstrikes on Iranian defence systems, sending ripples across the Gulf, but Trump insists they are “minor strikes” while intense diplomatic efforts continue to avert an all-out war.
summary: The US military carried out new airstrikes on Iranian defence systems. Trump insists the strikes are minor while diplomatic efforts continue to avert an all‑out war.
author: Euronews

title: Pope Leo XIV Welcomed by 40,000 in Paysandú, Uruguay
content: The Pontiff was welcomed by 40,000 people in Paysandú, Uruguay. Leo's sixth apostolic journey comes less than a month after lung adenocarcinoma surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital.
summary: Pope Leo XIV was welcomed by 40,000 people in Paysandú, Uruguay. The visit is his sixth apostolic journey and occurs less than a month after his lung adenocarcinoma surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital.
author: Euronews

title: Video shows people fleeing during gunman shooting in Kraków, Poland
content: Video footage captured on user‑generated content shows people running for cover amid a deadly shooting in Kraków, Poland. According to police, the incident has resulted in at least six fatalities and around a dozen injuries.
summary: UGC footage shows people running for cover during a deadly shooting in Kraków, Poland. Police say at least six people were killed and around a dozen were wounded.
author: Euronews

title: Russian strikes damage Kyiv region infrastructure, ruin kindergarten in capital
content: Russian strikes have damaged infrastructure in the Kyiv region and left a kindergarten in ruins in the Ukrainian capital. Firefighters battled a major blaze as Ukraine faced renewed attacks on its energy network.
summary: Russian strikes damaged infrastructure in the Kyiv region and left a kindergarten in ruins in the Ukrainian capital. Firefighters battled a major blaze as Ukraine faced renewed attacks on its energy network.
author: Euronews

title: Footage shows gunman shooting in Krakow's Main Market Square, six dead
content: Footage captured a shooting at Krakow’s Main Market Square, showing a gunman opening fire. People were seen taking cover and fleeing while cars sped away. The attack left six people dead and about 15 injured.
summary: Footage shows people fleeing and cars speeding away during a shooting at Krakow's Main Market Square. The incident left six people dead and about 15 injured.
author: Euronews

title: Trump offers UFC head Dana White White House press secretary role
content: After a series of combative press briefings between the Trump administration and journalists, the US president surprised many by reportedly offering Dana White, the head of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) and a longtime friend, the role of White House press secretary. Trump praised White as a “violent fighter and warrior”, but US media reports say he has already turned down the offer. Was it a punchy choice by the president or simply a punchline? Jack Pownall takes a closer look.
summary: President Trump reportedly offered Dana White, head of the UFC, the role of White House press secretary. Media reports say White has already turned down the offer.
author: France 24

title: Israeli President Herzog Tasks Gadi Eisenkot to Form Government
content:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog officially tasked former military chief Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government after neither Eisenkot’s bloc nor incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured a clear majority in the October 27 elections.  

Eisenkot now has up to six weeks to assemble a coalition government.  Follow our liveblog to see how the day’s events unfold.
summary: On Sunday, Israeli President Isaac Herzog officially tasked former military chief Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government. Eisenkot has up to six weeks to build a coalition after neither his bloc nor incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured a clear majority in the October 27 elections.
author: France 24

title: Paraguay Senate Impeaches President Santiago Peña After He Offered Resignation
content:
Paraguay’s Senate impeached ousted President Santiago Peña instead of accepting his offer to resign. Peña was charged over the collapse of Ueno Bank, an online bank where regulators seized control after nearly three million customers were locked out of their accounts. While repayments are currently underway, protests persist as customers continue to demand access to their funds.

Peña, who denies any wrongdoing, was initially placed under house arrest before being transferred to a military facility for his own safety.
summary: Paraguay's Senate impeached ousted president Santiago Peña after he offered to resign, and he has been charged over the collapse of Ueno Bank. He was moved from house arrest to a military facility for safety while nearly three million customers remain locked out of their accounts, with repayments beginning amid protests; Peña denies any wrongdoing.
author: France 24

title: Diwali celebrations see over one billion participants worldwide
content: Diwali celebrations began on Sunday, with people across India and the global diaspora gathering to mark one of the most important festivals in the Hindu tradition. According to the headline, over one billion people are observing the festival as a victory of light over darkness. In Ayodhya, the site traditionally regarded as the birthplace of Lord Rama, festivities featured performances based on the Hindu epic Ramayana, along with laser and light shows, live music, fireworks and drone displays.
summary: Diwali celebrations began on Sunday as people across India and the global diaspora gathered for the Hindu festival. In Ayodhya, believed to be Lord Rama's birthplace, events featured Ramayana performances, laser and light shows, live music, fireworks and drone displays.
author: France 24

title: Senegal Wins Two Beach Wrestling Golds at 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games
content: Senegal won two gold medals in beach wrestling at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. Elisabeth Diatta won gold in the -55 kg category, the host country’s first gold medal at the Youth Olympic Games. Her compatriot Maguette Diop followed suit, taking gold in the -80 kg category.
summary: Senegal secured two gold medals in beach wrestling at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. Elisabeth Diatta won the -55 kg gold, the host country’s first Youth Olympic gold, and Maguette Diop won gold in the -80 kg category.
author: France 24

title: Pope Leo XIV arrives in Argentina, criticises Milei's three-year austerity
content: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Argentina on Sunday from Uruguay, where his tour began, becoming the first pontiff to visit the late Pope Francis’ homeland in nearly four decades. He faced calls to help bridge divisions after three years of austerity under President Javier Milei, publicly criticizing that policy and stating that economic growth must benefit all.
summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Buenos Aires on Sunday, after beginning his tour in Uruguay. The first papal visit to the late Pope Francis’ homeland in nearly four decades, he criticised President Javier Milei’s three‑year austerity programme and said economic growth must benefit all.
author: France 24

title: Nvidia board to investigate reports Chinese intelligence targeted CEO Jensen Huang
content: Nvidia’s board announced on Sunday it will investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The New York Times reported Huang had an affair with an executive that U.S. intelligence believed was gathering information for Beijing. Huang will remain CEO during the inquiry and has pledged cooperation.
summary: Nvidia’s board said Sunday it would investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The New York Times reported Huang had an affair with an executive US intelligence believed was gathering information for Beijing, and he will remain CEO during the inquiry and has pledged cooperation.
author: France 24

title: Trump vows political comeback after GOP loses Congress, Democrats pledge accountability
content: President Donald Trump said on Sunday that he intends to make a political comeback after Republicans lost control of Congress in Tuesday’s midterm elections. Incoming Democratic leaders said they will hold his administration to account, while the attorney general pledged to defend officials against threatened prosecutions.
summary: President Donald Trump said on Sunday he will seek a political comeback after Republicans lost control of Congress in the recent midterm elections. Incoming Democratic leaders said they will hold his administration to account, and the attorney general promised to defend officials against threatened prosecutions.
author: France 24

title: Gaza siblings born without legs receive first personal chair
content:
In Gaza, 10‑year‑old Anas is one of three siblings born without legs and with only two fingers on each hand. They struggle to move around and to perform daily tasks such as eating and writing independently.

For the first time, one of the siblings has their own chair, a development that brings a new sense of freedom to the family.
summary: In Gaza, 10‑year‑old Anas is one of three siblings born without legs and with only two fingers on each hand. The children struggle to move around and perform daily activities such as eating and writing independently.
author: UN News

title: Beyond the broken glass: The human cost of the 1938 November Pogrom
content: On his way to school in Vienna on the morning of 10 November 1938, eight-year-old Arthur Schneier watched his synagogue burn while firefighters and police officers stood by “rejoicing”.
summary: Beyond the broken glass: The human cost of the 1938 November Pogrom.
author: UN News

title: GPs to provide extra support to 300,000 vulnerable patients in £40m NHS winter scheme
content:
A £40 million scheme in England will provide extra support to vulnerable patients in an effort to ease winter pressure on the NHS. Family doctors will extend services to 300,000 people with frailty and long‑term conditions, offering health checks, medication reviews and respiratory tests aimed at preventing avoidable hospital admissions.

The programme is intended to keep most vulnerable individuals well at home and reduce unnecessary stays in hospital as the NHS prepares for the coming months’ demands.
summary: A £40 million scheme in England will have family doctors offer extra support to 300,000 vulnerable patients this winter. The support includes health checks, medication reviews and respiratory tests aimed at preventing avoidable hospital admissions.
author: Guardian World

title: Education Secretary Lucy Powell warns early GCSE teaching may turn schools into exam factories
content: Lucy Powell says proposals to end widespread practice will be included in overhaul of England’s national curriculum Pushing GCSE subjects on younger pupils risks turning England’s secondary schools into “early exam factories”, the education secretary has said, warning that it is increasing disengagement from education. Lucy Powell wants schools to end the widespread practice of teaching GCSE topics to pupils in year 9 or earlier, before they officially start in year 10, and says she plans to reduce the amount of GCSE content to make it easier to fit into the official timetable.
summary: Education Secretary Lucy Powell warns early GCSE teaching may turn schools into exam factories.
author: Guardian World

title: Maya Jama steps down as Love Island host after nine seasons
content: ‘Time to throw myself into something new,’ 32-year-old presenter announces on social media while hailing her ‘unforgettable time’ on the show Maya Jama has announced she is stepping down as the host of Love Island after three years. The 32-year-old presenter of the reality TV show made the announcement on Instagram.
summary: Maya Jama, a 32‑year‑old presenter, announced on Instagram that she is leaving her role as host of Love Island. She said it is time to throw herself into something new after three years on the show.
author: Guardian World

title: Earthshot prize ceremony set for Reliance-owned Jio World Centre in Mumbai, draws criticism
content:
Conservation groups have voiced criticism of the venue chosen for the Prince of Wales’s Earthshot prize awards. The ceremony will be held on 17 November at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai, a facility owned by Reliance Industries, the conglomerate of the Ambani family that operates the world’s largest oil refinery and funds a controversial mega‑zoo.  

A spokesperson for the Earthshot prize, which grants £1 million each year to five winners for conservation projects, confirmed the location to the Guardian and Mongabay. The criticism centres on Reliance’s fossil‑fuel interests and the zoo project linked to its foundation.
summary: The Prince of Wales’s Earthshot prize will hold its annual awards ceremony on 17 November at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai. Conservationists have criticised the venue because it is owned by Reliance Industries, which runs the world’s biggest oil refinery and funds a controversial mega‑zoo.
author: Guardian World

title: Court rejects Home Office claim asylum seeker ransom kidnapping not trafficking
content:
The Court of Appeal rejected the Home Office’s claim that kidnapping for ransom does not constitute exploitation of trafficking victims. The decision was reached in a case involving a Syrian man who was abducted in Libya.

With the ruling, people who have been kidnapped for ransom—previously excluded from the definition of trafficking victims—will now have their claims considered. Those individuals may become eligible for the support and recovery package that is available to recognized trafficking victims.
summary: Court rejects Home Office claim asylum seeker ransom kidnapping not trafficking.
author: Guardian World

title: President Isaac Herzog tasks Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming Israeli government
content: Israel’s president has tasked Yashar party leader Gadi Eiskont with attempting to form a new government after the Knesset remained deadlocked following last month’s election, which saw Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition lose its majority. The president’s office, headed by Isaac Herzog, said Herzog informed Eisenkot on Saturday night of his intention to assign him the mandate. Eisenkot is described as Netanyahu’s strongest rival in the race to lead the next administration.
summary: The Knesset has been deadlocked since the election last month when Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition lost its majority. President Isaac Herzog informed Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu’s strongest rival, that he will be tasked with forming a new government.
author: Guardian World

title: Wagga Wagga family members charged as accessories after the fact in Danielle Madgwick murder
content:
Danielle Madgwick, a 23‑year‑old woman, died in regional New South Wales in September after suffering multiple stab wounds to her upper body. Emergency services responded to a Wagga Wagga home on the morning of 19 September, where they found Madgwick with the injuries and she died at the scene.

Family members of a man accused of the domestic‑violence murder of Madgwick have been charged with being accessories after the fact to the alleged crime. The charges relate to the alleged murder that occurred in south‑western New South Wales.
summary: Family members of a man accused of murdering 23‑year‑old Danielle Madgwick in south‑western New South Wales have been charged with being accessories after the fact. Emergency services found Madgwick with multiple stab wounds at a Wagga Wagga home on the morning of 19 September, and she died at the scene.
author: Guardian World

title: Beau Lamarre-Condon denies executing Jesse Baird while reenacting shooting in NSW court
content:
Former police officer Beau Lamarre‑Condon pleaded not guilty to the murders of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Paddington in early 2024. In a Sydney court, he told the judge that he did not “execute” Baird and that he was unaware of a “massive” gunshot wound to the 26‑year‑old’s face.

Lamarre‑Condon is accused of fatally shooting Baird and Davies with his police service weapon at Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024. During the NSW trial, he reenacted the shooting while giving evidence. The article contains graphic content.
summary: Former police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon has pleaded not guilty to the murders of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Paddington. In a Sydney court he said he did not “execute” Baird, was unaware of the massive gunshot wound to Baird’s face, and reenacted the shooting while giving evidence.
author: Guardian World

title: NASA chief Isaacman: US will launch big rockets yearly to beat China in lunar race
content:
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman has expressed strong confidence in the agency’s Artemis program, stating that the United States is on a more achievable path to the lunar surface than in previous years. This optimism follows the success of the Artemis II mission, which orbited the moon in April 2026. In a recent interview with Space.com, Isaacman highlighted that the recent announcement of Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman becoming the new deputy director of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory reflects the program’s momentum. However, Isaacman emphasized that the journey toward crewed lunar landings and a permanent moon base requires consistent execution, specifically launching NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) megarocket no less than once a year.

Isaacman stated that while the space community often debates the readiness of lunar landers, his current priority is the frequency of SLS launches. He noted that the upcoming Artemis III mission, scheduled for 2027, will be a crewed flight to low Earth orbit designed to test docking procedures between NASA’s Orion capsule and private lunar landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin. Isaacman described these annual launches as imperative for deep-space human spaceflight, arguing that while the agency may not return to the high launch rates of the Apollo or early shuttle eras, an annual cadence is the minimum standard to justify the risks and taxpayer dollars involved. He added that this consistent activity is essential to better prepare the agency for Artemis IV, which is targeted for 2028.

The Artemis program is being driven by a renewed space race with China, a dynamic Isaacman described as distinct from the Cold War competition with the Soviet Union. While the United States held significant technological advantages in computing and other domains during the 1960s, Isaacman noted that current capabilities are much closer. He pointed out that while NASA aims to land on the moon by the end of 2028, China has stated its goal is to achieve this by the end of 2029. Isaacman acknowledged that China is likely to succeed in its lunar ambitions, citing the country’s showcased landers, rovers, suits, and two-launch architecture with built-in reusability.

Isaacman stressed that NASA is taking the Chinese threat seriously, warning that failing to meet its lunar goals would have severe global consequences. He suggested that a loss in this race could cast doubt on American technological superiority, influencing global decisions regarding the use of American versus Chinese artificial intelligence, computers, vehicles, and security guarantees. Despite these challenges, Isaacman expressed confidence in the agency’s ability to succeed, citing the enduring spirit, energy, and talent within NASA and its industry partners as comparable to the workforce of the 1960s. He concluded that while the approach differs from the Apollo era, the agency possesses a "playbook of success" and believes it will prevail in the current lunar competition.
summary: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition.
author: Space.com

title: Usman Khawaja defends timing of ball-tampering revelations
content:
Usman Khawaja has defended the timing of his ball-tampering revelations, insisting he has not thrown anyone under the bus. The former Test opener addressed the controversy on social media one day after claiming that sandpaper was used in the Test prior to Cape Town 2018. Khawaja stated that the entire team was responsible for the incident.

In his explanation, Khawaja said he would “not deny” that everyone knew about the use of sandpaper. His bombshell claims have since rocked Australian cricket, prompting his recent defense of why he chose to release the information at this specific time.
summary: Usman Khawaja stated he has not thrown anyone under the bus while defending the timing of his claims about sandpaper use in the Test prior to Cape Town 2018. He explained on social media that he would not deny everyone knew about the incident and that the entire team was responsible.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Alan Jones, 80, Former Formula One Champion, Dies
content: Australian driver who was the Formula One champion with the Williams team in 1981 and had 12 grand prix victories “The championship? You take it any way it comes,” said Alan Jones, with typical unsentimental pithiness, after winning a tense Canadian Grand Prix in Montreal in 1980 that made him that year’s Formula One world champion. This came during his third season with the Williams Grand Prix team, after making a promising showing the year before with four race victories. Jones, who has died aged 80 of cancer, had taken full advantage of the aerodynamic excellence of the new Williams FW07 car, featuring revolutionary “ground effect” technology, which was introduced in the latter part of the 1979 season.
summary: Alan Jones, an Australian driver, was the 1981 Formula One champion with the Williams team and had 12 grand prix victories. Jones died aged 80 of cancer.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Anjali Doshi: Rising sexist abuse in cricket journalism
content:
Anjali Doshi, a cricket reporter with two decades of experience, states that the abuse she has faced in recent years is shocking and demoralizing. In an article for Wisden Cricket Monthly, she reflects on her first experience covering an India versus England one-day international at the Wankhede press box twenty-four years ago. On that occasion, England won by five runs after Andrew Flintoff sprinted across the outfield twirling his shirt, a moment that reportedly annoyed captain Sourav Ganguly.

At the time, Doshi was one of only two women in the press contingent. She describes writing her report for the local tabloid, the Afternoon Despatch & Courier, with trepidation and a sense of impostor syndrome. She was terrified about how her male peers and senior colleagues would perceive her presence and work. The piece highlights that while female sports journalists have always faced sexism, social media has made the harassment vicious and relentless.
summary: Anjali Doshi has reported on cricket for twenty years and has experienced shocking and demoralising abuse in recent years. She first entered the Wankhede press box 24 years ago as one of only two women, writing for the Afternoon Despatch & Courier amid fears of male peers' reactions.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England's Steve Borthwick leads team to record victory over Australia
content:
Andy Bull reports that England’s recent win over Australia was a record‑setting, blue‑riband victory.  The match, described as a “demolition” of the Australian side, was the best performance England has delivered since Steve Borthwick took over, and the best since the team beat New Zealand at Twickenham last year.

Borthwick’s side were noted for playing without excuses or apologies, presenting a finished, arrogant, imposing performance.  The commentators highlighted a few early errors – “silly scrum penalties” and “shonky lineout throws” – but said these did not detract from the overall quality of the game.

The article ends with Borthwick smiling after the match, signalling a moment of satisfaction for the head coach and his squad.
summary: England beat Australia in a record victory, with Steve Borthwick's team described as arrogant, imposing and excellent. It was one of England's best games since Borthwick took over as head coach, following a win over New Zealand last year.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Emotion gets better of Samoa as Australia begin to resemble their old selves | Angus Fontaine
content:
Australia’s Kangaroos secured a semi‑final victory over Samoa, a match that saw the Samoan side arrive in Sydney with strong Pasifika passion but ultimately be outplayed. The game ended with Australia advancing, while Samoa’s hopes were described as washed away like tears in the city’s rain.

Samoa’s campaign was marked by pride and passion, with large crowds of supporters following the team around the nation. The players, a diamond‑league diaspora of NRL stars honouring ancestral ties, served that fanbase nobly throughout the month. The emotion of playing for those supporters, however, proved to be a decisive factor.

Both tiny island nations—Samoa and fellow semi‑finalists Tonga—were represented with enthusiasm, yet the larger Pacific teams, Australia and New Zealand, moved on to the final on maturity and composure.
summary: Emotion gets better of Samoa as Australia begin to resemble their old selves | Angus Fontaine.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Lando Norris wins São Paulo Grand Prix, Mercedes clinch ninth constructors' title
content:
Lando Norris delivered a masterclass for victory at the São Paulo Grand Prix, taking the flag at a meeting marked by a series of striking comebacks.  

Max Verstappen was once more outstanding at Interlagos, moving from 21st on the grid to finish second, and for McLaren it was a victory they have sought since mid‑season.  

Mercedes wrapped up the constructors’ championship, claiming their ninth Formula One constructors’ world championship and confirming a definitive return from the wilderness.
summary: Lando Norris won the São Paulo Grand Prix after a masterclass performance, while Max Verstappen moved from 21st on the grid to finish second. Mercedes secured their ninth Formula One constructors’ world championship at the event.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Patrick Dorgu scores 96th‑minute equaliser as Man United draw 4‑4 with Aston Villa
content:
The match ended in an eight‑goal thriller, with Patrick Dorgu scoring a 96th‑minute equaliser for Manchester United. The goal came from a header off his head after a corner set up by Senne Lammens, with Zion Suzuki as the opposite number; no foul was awarded, a decision that upset Aston Villa manager Unai Emery. Michael Carrick had urged United to build momentum following a breathless comeback win over Roma.

The equaliser made the score 4‑4, before Joshua Zirkzee’s added‑time finish for Villa pulled the visitors back. Carrick’s “chaotic unit” was credited with preventing defeat, leaving his job in question after the late draw.
summary: Patrick Dorgu’s 96th‑minute header equalised the match at 4‑4, giving Manchester United a point against Aston Villa. The goal followed a corner in which Senne Lammens collided with Zion Suzuki without a foul being given, a decision that displeased Villa manager Unai Emery, and Joshua Zirkzee also scored in added time.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Feyi-Waboso's blistering first half sparks hope for England under Borthwick
content: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso delivered a blistering first-half performance, offering England supporters a preview of the team's potential under coach Steve Borthwick. The display provides a basis for a much-needed statement of faith in Borthwick’s leadership.
summary: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso delivered a blistering first half for England. The performance offers fans a glimpse of a potential statement of faith in coach Steve Borthwick.
author: BBC Sport

title: Sunderland beat Chelsea to lift from bottom of Premier League
content: Sunderender secured their first Premier League victory since August by defeating Chelsea at the Stadium of Light. The win, assisted by Enzo le Fee's penalty, allowed the hosts to move off the bottom of the league table.
summary: Sunderland earned their first Premier League win since August by beating Chelsea. Enzo le Fee's penalty helped the hosts sink the visitors at the Stadium of Light.
author: BBC Sport

title: Brighton beat 10-man Brentford 2-0 to move up to second in Premier League
content: Diego Gomez’s long-range strike secured a 2-0 victory for Brighton against Brentford. Brentford’s Igor Thiago received a straight red card during the match. The win allows Fabian Hurzeler’s Brighton side to move up to second place in the Premier League.
summary: Diego Gomez scored a long-range strike as Brighton defeated Brentford 2-0. Brentford's Igor Thiago received a straight red card during the match.
author: BBC Sport

title: Man Utd score twice in stoppage time to share points in eight-goal thriller
content: Manchester United and Aston Villa shared points in an eight-goal thriller at Old Trafford, with the hosts scoring twice in stoppage time to complete a comeback from two goals down. Despite securing a draw, Manchester United will enter the Premier League international break positioned in the relegation zone.
summary: Manchester United came back from two goals down to earn a point against Aston Villa in an eight-goal thriller at Old Trafford. They will go into the international break in the Premier League relegation zone.
author: BBC Sport

title: Florida Gov.-elect Byron Donalds urges GOP to craft healthcare policy for 2028
content: Florida Gov.-elect Byron Donalds (R) told Fox News’s “Sunday Morning Futures” host Larry Kudlow that the Republican Party must develop its own healthcare policy for the 2028 election. Donalds said Republican lawmakers on Capitol Hill are having “many debates” about taking on healthcare.
summary: Florida Gov.-elect Byron Donalds said the Republican Party must develop its own healthcare policy for the 2028 election. He told Fox News’s Larry Kudlow that Capitol Hill lawmakers are debating healthcare issues.
author: The Hill

title: NYC Mayor Mamdani says abolishing ICE is most acceptable DSA platform item
content:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, said that among the party’s platform items the most “acceptable” to mainstream America is the abolition of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).  
Mamdani appeared on “Fox News Sunday” for an interview recorded Wednesday night.
summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) said that abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is the most acceptable part of the Democratic Socialists of America platform for mainstream America. He appeared on Fox News Sunday for an interview recorded Wednesday night.
author: The Hill

title: Trump says unlikely to renew attacks on Iran if talks progress
content: President Trump said he was “highly unlikely” to renew attacks against Iran if upcoming peace talks show progress on Tehran’s nuclear program and the opening of the Strait of Hormuz, according to a new CNN report. He added, “It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement,” during an interview with CNN’s Jim Sciutto.
summary: President Trump said he was highly unlikely to renew attacks against Iran if peace talks show progress on Tehran’s nuclear program and opening the Strait of Hormuz. He added that it depends on whether a very strong agreement is signed, according to an interview with CNN’s Jim Sciutto.
author: The Hill

title: Iran Issues Two-Day Diplomacy Ultimatum to US
content: Iran issued a two‑day diplomatic ultimatum to the United States. On Sunday, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi warned that Tehran’s latest offer to end the more than eight‑month war must be accepted or else face military escalation. He added that President Trump is mulling further strikes after the midterms and urged the White House to act, noting that “American voters have made their choice.”
summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Sunday warned the U. S.
author: The Hill

title: Nvidia Board Opens Investigation into CEO Jensen Huang Over Alleged Spy Relationship
content: Nvidia’s board of directors announced that it would open an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang. The move follows reports that Huang allegedly had an intimate relationship with a woman whom U.S. intelligence officials believe was spying for China. The board said it is reviewing the recent reporting that raises these concerns.
summary: Nvidia’s board of directors announced it would be opening an investigation into its CEO, Jensen Huang, following reports alleging he had an intimate relationship with a woman U. S.
author: The Hill

title: Richard Walters departs as White House deputy chief of staff after Stephen Miller's promotion
content: White House deputy chief of staff Richard Walters is departing from his role in the wake of longtime Trump adviser Stephen Miller being announced as the new chief of staff. “Richard has been an invaluable member of the White House and has helped deliver some of the Administration’s biggest victories,” Miller said in a statement…
summary: Richard Walters, the White House deputy chief of staff, is leaving his position. His departure follows the announcement that Stephen Miller will become the new chief of staff.
author: The Hill

title: Congress returns after midterm losses; Republicans battle for House leadership.
content: Congress has returned to Capitol Hill after a midterm election that delivered major losses to Republicans and left Democrats in a strong position. Republicans now face a key test: a leadership battle as the party prepares to move into minority status. House Republicans are scheduled to hold leadership elections, and a shutdown deadline looms following the GOP losses.
summary: Congress returns to Capitol Hill after a midterm election that caused major Republican losses and boosted Democrats. Republicans now face a leadership contest as they prepare to move into the House minority.
author: The Hill

title: Democrats Seek New Path to Expand Senate Majority in 2028
content: Democrats’ sweeping victory on Tuesday has upended conventional expectations about the 2028 Senate map. Party leaders now view the future as an open field, aiming to broaden their majority. They note that several states where they secured wins this election could provide fresh opportunities for expansion.
summary: Democrats' sweeping victory Tuesday has scrambled conventional wisdom about the 2028 Senate map. Party leaders are looking to expand their majority, noting that some of the very same states where they won this election could offer new opportunities.
author: The Hill

title: NPR interview examines Democrats' foreign policy direction after midterm win
content: NPR host Rob Schmitz interviewed Thomas Wright, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, regarding Wright’s recent Foreign Affairs article, “The Fight for the Future of Democratic Foreign Policy.” The conversation focused on the piece’s analysis of how Democrats might shape U.S. foreign policy following their midterm election victory.
summary: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Thomas Wright, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution. They discuss Wright's Foreign Affairs article titled The Fight for the Future of Democratic Foreign Policy.
author: NPR Politics

title: Heavy rain floods around 70,000 tents in Gaza, worsening humanitarian situation
content:
Heavy rain began hitting Gaza on Saturday, marking the start of the first winter storm affecting the territory. Within 12 hours, reports indicated that roughly 70,000 tents used by displaced families were flooded.

Humanitarian officials warned that the flooding could worsen conditions for hundreds of thousands of people living in temporary camps that lack adequate protection from rain and cold.
summary: Heavy rain began hitting Gaza on Saturday, marking the first winter storm affecting the area. About 70,000 tents were flooded within 12 hours, prompting warnings of a worsening humanitarian situation for hundreds of thousands of displaced people in temporary camps lacking adequate protection.
author: Guardian Environment

title: US records over 5,000 measles cases, highest in 35 years
content: The United States has recorded more than 5,000 measles cases this year, the highest number in 35 years, according to an official count released on Friday. The data reflects the nation’s most severe measles outbreak in three and a half decades.
summary: The United States has recorded more than 5,000 measles cases this year. This is the highest number in 35 years, according to an official count released Friday.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study identifies unknown mechanism driving therapy resistance in advanced prostate cancer
content: A multi‑institutional collaborative study led by researchers at the University of Chicago and the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center has identified a previously unknown biological mechanism that controls cell identity and treatment resistance in advanced prostate cancer.
summary: A multi‑institutional collaborative study led by researchers at the University of Chicago and the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center identified a previously unknown biological mechanism. The mechanism controls cell identity and treatment resistance in advanced prostate cancer.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study finds higher parkinsonism rates in middle‑aged and older adults with autism
content: A new study finds that middle‑aged and older adults with autism are more likely to have co‑occurring parkinsonism than adults without autism or intellectual disability. The research was led by George Washington University investigators in the Department of Speech, Language and Hearing Sciences.
summary: Researchers at George Washington University’s Department of Speech, Language and Hearing Sciences reported that middle‑aged and older adults with autism are more likely to have co‑occurring parkinsonism than adults without autism or intellectual disability. The study compared these groups to adults lacking autism and intellectual disability.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Earth's gravity may have sustained early moon's volcanic activity
content:
New analysis of lunar material brought back by China’s Chang’e‑5 mission shows that some of the rock formed about 2 billion years ago and bears characteristics of volcanic origin. This finding challenges the conventional view that the Moon cooled quickly after the giant impact that created it around 4.5 billion years ago, leaving only occasional asteroid impacts to modify its surface.

Researchers suggest that Earth’s gravity may have helped sustain the Moon’s early volcanic activity longer than expected, allowing magma to erupt as late as 2 billion years ago. The Chang’e‑5 samples provide direct evidence that volcanic processes persisted well after the Moon’s initial formation.
summary: The moon is generally thought to have cooled quickly after forming from a giant impact with Earth about 4.5 billion years ago. However, lunar material returned by the Chang'e‑5 mission dates to roughly 2 billion years ago and shows evidence of volcanic origin, suggesting Earth’s gravity may have kept the moon’s interior active.
author: Phys.org

title: Hybrid trapped-ion quantum computer simulates Aharonov‑Bohm effect in lattice gauge theory
content: A recent Nature Physics paper reports that researchers have used a hybrid trapped‑ion quantum computer to simulate a lattice gauge theory and observe the Aharonov‑Bohm effect. The study demonstrates interference arising from magnetic flux in the simulated system.
summary: Researchers demonstrated the Aharonov‑Bohm effect in a quantum simulation of a lattice gauge theory. The demonstration used a hybrid trapped‑ion quantum computer and was reported in a new Nature Physics study.
author: Phys.org

title: Different genres enable doctoral students to tailor writing for new audiences
content:
Different text genres place distinct demands on writers. An academic abstract, a blog post, and a public outreach article each require a unique approach.

Readers’ prior knowledge, the purpose of the text, and what needs explaining vary across these genres. Consequently, mastering one type of writing does not automatically equip a doctoral student to write another effectively.
summary: Academic abstracts, blog posts and public outreach articles each place distinct demands on writers. Because readers’ prior knowledge, text purpose and explanatory needs vary, mastering one genre does not automatically ensure ability to write another.
author: Phys.org

title: Insects provide diverse ecosystem services beyond food, from pollination to waste decomposition
content: Insects number at least 14 million species worldwide and sustain the natural world through highly diverse roles. Scientists refer to their contributions as “ecosystem services.” For instance, bees and hoverflies pollinate wildflowers and agricultural crops, while dung beetles decompose manure and other waste materials.
summary: There are at least 14 million insect species on Earth that perform many ecosystem services. Bees and hoverflies pollinate wildflowers and agricultural crops, and dung beetles decompose manure and other waste materials.
author: Phys.org

title: Student documents rare wild cat in Carson National Forest, NM
content: William Grooms used dozens of motion‑sensing cameras during the summer to document wildlife across Carson National Forest in northern New Mexico. This was his first field season collecting photos for a two‑year study aimed at understanding how forest structure influences biodiversity in the Southern Rocky Mountains.
summary: William Grooms, a student, captured evidence of a rare wild cat in Carson National Forest in northern New Mexico. He used dozens of motion‑sensing cameras during his first summer field season for a two‑year study of how forest structure influences biodiversity in the Southern Rocky Mountains.
author: Phys.org

title: Space weather drives auroras and poses risk to power grids
content: An aurora appears as green or red curtains rippling across the night sky, producing a spectacular light show. When viewed from the ground, the display may seem far away and disconnected from anything happening on Earth’s surface. The title notes that space weather powers these auroras and also threatens power grids on the ground.
summary: An aurora appears as green or red curtains rippling across the night sky. The same space weather that powers these light displays can also threaten power grids on the ground.
author: Phys.org

title: JWST finds 104 magnified stellar events in Dragon galaxy, doubling prior record
content:
The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) enabled a team of astronomers to identify 104 magnified stellar events in the Dragon galaxy, located roughly 6.5 billion light‑years from Earth. This count more than doubles the prior record of 44 such detections in the same galaxy.

These magnified events highlight some of the most luminous stars and suggest the presence of dark matter. The study therefore provides a rare glimpse of the Dragon’s stellar population and offers a potential clue to the nature of dark matter.
summary: Using JWST, astronomers identified 104 magnified stellar events in the Dragon galaxy about 6.5 billion light‑years away. The count more than doubles the previous record of 44 detections and offers a rare view of the galaxy’s luminous stars and a possible hint of dark matter.
author: Phys.org

title: Liquid-assisted crystal growth cuts perovskite defects for efficient solar cells and LEDs
content: A research team led by Professor Seong Sik Shin of the SKKU Advanced Institute of Nanotechnology at Sungkyunkwan University, working with the Korea Research Institute of Chemical Technology, the University of California, San Diego and Princeton University, has created a next‑generation perovskite semiconductor thin film that exhibits dramatically reduced defects. The team employed a liquid‑assisted crystal‑growth method to achieve the lower defect density. Using this same material platform, they demonstrated both high‑performance solar cells and light‑emitting diodes.
summary: Liquid-assisted crystal growth cuts perovskite defects for efficient solar cells and LEDs.
author: Phys.org

title: Broccoli compound may aid treatment of Friedreich ataxia
content: Scientists have identified a naturally occurring compound in broccoli that may combat Friedreich ataxia, a genetic disease that progressively harms the nervous system. The compound appears to boost a vital protein and protect nerve cells, raising hopes for an affordable therapy. However, clinical trials are still required to confirm its effectiveness in patients.
summary: A compound naturally found in broccoli could help fight Friedreich ataxia by boosting a vital protein and protecting nerve cells. Scientists hope the discovery could lead to an affordable treatment, but clinical trials are still needed to confirm its effectiveness in patients.
author: Science Daily

title: Low testosterone tied to 18% higher cancer death risk in study of 26,000 men
content: A large international study that followed more than 26,000 men found that men with very low testosterone levels faced an 18 % higher risk of dying from cancer later in life. The analysis showed no clear association between testosterone levels and prostate cancer, although two other sex hormones were linked to that disease. Researchers noted that testosterone levels falling below 8.6 nmol/L might serve as an early warning sign of future health risks.
summary: A major international study tracking more than 26,000 men found that very low testosterone levels were associated with an 18% higher risk of dying from cancer later in life. Surprisingly, testosterone itself showed no clear link to prostate cancer, although two other sex hormones did.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find structural brain changes linked to common sleep disorders
content: Scientists report that sleep disorders are linked to structural changes in brain regions governing attention, decision‑making and emotions, which may explain how disrupted sleep influences everyday thinking and behavior. The conclusion comes from an analysis of 57 brain‑imaging studies that identified both shared and disorder‑specific patterns, suggesting potential pathways for more targeted treatments.
summary: Scientists discovered that sleep disorders are associated with structural changes in brain regions that control attention, decision-making, and emotions. The findings, drawn from 57 brain imaging studies, reveal both shared and disorder-specific patterns that could lead to more targeted treatments.
author: Science Daily

title: Humans emit over 2 billion tonnes of CO2 yearly from metabolism, up 74% in 30 years
content: Humans collectively exhale more than 2 billion metric tons of carbon dioxide each year as they convert food into energy, a level that has risen 74 % over the past three decades, primarily due to population growth. Because this CO₂ is part of the natural carbon cycle rather than fossil‑fuel emissions, scientists say that more precise measurement of human respiration could help refine climate models.
summary: Humans collectively produce more than 2 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide each year by converting food into energy, a 74% increase over three decades driven largely by population growth. Scientists note that this exhaled CO2 is part of the natural carbon cycle and that better measurement could improve climate models.
author: Science Daily

title: Psilocybin shown to rapidly create and strengthen new brain connections in mice
content: Scientists have discovered that psilocybin, the active compound in magic mushrooms, can rapidly reshape the brain by generating new neural connections and strengthening existing ones. In experiments with mice, the drug exhibited different effects in healthy animals compared to those experiencing chronic stress, suggesting it may help repair brain circuits damaged by prolonged stress. The researchers also identified a method to induce this neural rewiring without producing the behavioral response typically linked to psychedelic effects.
summary: Researchers discovered that psilocybin rapidly reshapes the brain by forming new neural connections and strengthening them. The drug acted differently in healthy versus chronically stressed mice and could be triggered to induce rewiring without the behavioral response linked to psychedelic effects.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists generate record 300‑attosecond X‑ray flashes in tiny spot
content: Scientists have generated X‑ray flashes that last only 300 attoseconds and concentrate unprecedented power into an extremely small focal spot. The achievement is described as a breakthrough that may enable direct observation of electrons in motion and could allow control of the ultrafast processes underlying chemical reactions.
summary: Scientists have created record‑breaking X‑ray flashes lasting 300 attoseconds that concentrate enormous power into an incredibly tiny spot. The breakthrough could provide a new way to observe electrons in action and potentially control the ultrafast processes that drive chemical reactions.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find Europe was covered by open woodlands, meadows for 20 million years
content: Scientists have found that for more than 20 million years Europe was primarily covered by open woodlands, colorful meadows and large grazing animals, rather than the dense forests traditionally viewed as its natural state. The finding questions current reforestation plans, indicating that planting thick forests might damage the biodiversity that conservationists aim to preserve.
summary: Scientists uncovered evidence that Europe was dominated for more than 20 million years by open woodlands, colorful meadows and large grazing animals, not the dense forests long considered its natural state. The discovery challenges modern reforestation strategies, suggesting that planting thick forests could actually harm the biodiversity conservationists hope to protect.
author: Science Daily

title: MIT scientists create nanoparticles that reprogram immune cells to kill cancer in mice
content: MIT researchers have created nanoparticles that reprogram immune cells directly within the body, prompting them to attack cancer and harmful immune cells. In mouse studies, the approach eliminated tumors and reversed liver damage. The scientists say the method could simplify and lower the cost of immune therapies and expand treatment options for cancer and autoimmune diseases.
summary: MIT scientists have developed nanoparticles that reprogram immune cells directly inside the body to attack cancer and harmful immune cells, eliminating tumors and reversing liver damage in mouse experiments. The breakthrough could make powerful immune therapies dramatically simpler and less expensive while opening new possibilities for treating cancer and autoimmune diseases.
author: Science Daily

title: Rep‑elect Will Lawrence vows to push federal data center moratorium
content: Will Lawrence, who defeated better‑funded opponents to win Michigan’s 7th District congressional race, is now the district’s representative‑elect. He has announced plans to pursue a federal moratorium on data center construction.
summary: Will Lawrence is the representative‑elect for Michigan’s 7th District after beating better‑funded opponents. He says he will work to enact a federal moratorium on data center construction.
author: Wired

title: AI‑enhanced caregiver apps become more capable, but caregiver well‑being remains unsolved
content: Apps and platforms that assist family caregivers in managing loved‑ones’ needs are gaining new capabilities, including artificial‑intelligence features. However, the broader challenge of supporting caregivers’ own well‑being remains unresolved.
summary: The apps and platforms that help family caregivers manage their loved ones’ needs are becoming more capable. However, the broader issue of caregivers’ well‑being remains unsolved.
author: Wired

title: Fridge-hacking spree highlights IoT security risks to critical infrastructure
content: Recent hacks of blood‑lab systems and grocery‑store networks illustrate how basic security gaps in internet‑connected devices can threaten critical infrastructure. The growing “fridge‑hacking” spree is being described as a wake‑up call to address these IoT vulnerabilities.
summary: Recent hacks affecting blood labs and grocery stores are escalating. They show real risks to critical infrastructure from basic security lapses in internet-connected devices.
author: Wired

title: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's ties to Chinese spy
content:
Nvidia disclosed that its board of directors is launching an independent investigation concerning CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. The probe follows reports that Alice Huang was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on the company and that Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

The investigation will be overseen by a committee of independent directors assisted by outside independent counsel. In its statement, the board emphasized that U.S. national and economic security is a paramount priority for Nvidia.
summary: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's ties to Chinese spy.
author: The Verge

title: Epic Games Launcher gains SteamOS support, says communications director
content:
In October, Epic Games announced it was investigating how to make Fortnite compatible with Valve’s Linux‑based SteamOS. At that time the Epic Games Launcher was still in preview, and SteamOS was not listed among the supported distributions.

Communications Director Jake Jones has since confirmed that SteamOS will be supported, along with several other Linux distros, in a recent interview with GamingOnLinux.

Jones explained that the new Epic Games Launcher remains in preview and that the company intends to support as many Linux distributions as possible. He noted plans to include Fedora, SteamOS, Cachy, Omarchy, and more, and that the launcher will replace the AppImage with Debian/Ubuntu downloads.
summary: Epic Games Launcher, still in preview, is now confirmed to be compatible with Valve’s Linux‑based SteamOS. Communications Director Jake Jones said the launcher will also support other Linux distributions such as Fedora, Cachy, Omarchy, and more.
author: The Verge

title: Apps designed to curb doomscrolling and boost productive content
content: Breaking the habit of doomscrolling can be challenging, but a variety of apps are available that aim to redirect users toward more engaging and productive content. These tools are presented as alternatives to endless negative scrolling, offering ways to spend time on material that supports a healthier online experience.
summary: Breaking the cycle of doomscrolling is hard. Plenty of apps can help users spend more time on engaging and productive content.
author: TechCrunch

title: Pokémon card craze fuels scalper race as fans queue at London’s Forbidden Planet
content:
Fans seeking the newest Pokémon card releases are finding themselves priced out as a “cut‑throat” market, driven by hype that a young fan likened to “crypto”. The demand has turned card collecting into a race against scalpers, according to observations from the scene.

On a Friday before the 10 a.m. opening of the pop‑culture shop Forbidden Planet in central London, a line that began at 3 a.m. stretched past five other queues. Kai, who had been waiting since the early hours, said the crowd was roughly “50/50” fans and resellers despite the store’s strict sales policy.
summary: Fans trying to buy the latest Pokémon cards are being priced out in a cut‑throat market driven by hype likened to crypto. At the Friday 10 am opening of Forbidden Planet in central London, a line that started at 3 am was about half fans and half resellers, according to Kai.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Trump offers UFC boss Dana White White House press secretary position
content: Trump and White have forged a close relationship over the years, with Trump a regular attendee at UFC events and White having spoken at a number of the president's rallies.
summary: Trump offered UFC boss Dana White a role as White House press secretary. The two have a close relationship, with Trump regularly attending UFC events and White speaking at many of the president's rallies.
author: Euronews

title: Eisenkot given 28 days to form new Israeli government after elections
content: Netanyahu rival Eisenkot has been designated to try to form a new Israeli government after the recent elections. Under Israeli law, the appointed candidate has 28 days to assemble a coalition, and the president may extend this period by up to 14 days before assigning the mandate to another individual.
summary: Eisenkot, a rival of Netanyahu, has been tasked with forming a new government in Israel. He has 28 days to do so, and the president may extend the period by up to 14 days before assigning the mandate to another candidate.
author: Euronews

title: US forces strike bulk carrier in Gulf of Oman after crew ignored warnings
content: US forces reportedly struck a commercial bulk carrier in the Gulf of Oman after the crew ignored repeated warnings, according to the headline. The UKMTO maritime agency said late on Saturday that it had received a report of an incident involving a bulk carrier and military forces in the gulf.
summary: US forces struck a commercial bulk carrier in the Gulf of Oman after the crew ignored repeated warnings. The UKMTO said it had received a report of the incident involving the bulk carrier and military forces in the gulf.
author: Euronews

title: Pope Leo XIV ends Uruguay visit with women tribute, mass draws 50,000 in Florida
content:
Pope Leo XIV concluded his visit to Uruguay with a tribute to women before departing for Argentina.  

Tens of thousands gathered in Florida’s main square for the Mass under bright blue skies, some walking several kilometres to reach the site. The city’s population is about 40,000, yet the Vatican estimated 50,000 attendees.
summary: Pope Leo XIV concluded his Uruguay trip with a tribute to women before departing for Argentina. Tens of thousands, estimated at 50,000 by the Vatican, attended a Mass in Florida’s main square despite the city’s 40,000 population.
author: Euronews

title: Kraków's main square reopens a day after shooting that killed six
content: Kraków’s historic main square reopened to the public on Sunday, 8 November, just over 24 hours after a deadly shooting that left six people dead and 15 injured. Residents are lighting candles in memory of the victims, while bullet marks remain visible on café windows.
summary: Kraków's historic main square reopened to the public on Sunday, 8 November, just over 24 hours after a shooting left six people dead and 15 injured. Residents are lighting candles in memory of the victims, and bullet marks remain visible on café windows.
author: Euronews

title: Tens of thousands march in red through Amsterdam demanding stronger Dutch action on Gaza
content: A sea of red filled Amsterdam’s streets on Sunday, 8 November, as tens of thousands of demonstrators—many wearing red—marched through the city. The protest called on the Dutch government to adopt stronger measures against Israel concerning the war in Gaza.
summary: Tens of thousands of people, many dressed in red, marched through Amsterdam on Sunday 8 November. They urged the Dutch government to take stronger action against Israel over the war in Gaza.
author: Euronews

title: French tear gas use sparks calls to ban after menstrual disorder reports
content: French police have deployed tear gas extensively during recent protests across France, resulting in grievous injuries. Thousands of women have reported acutely painful periods and increased bleeding, challenging the assumption that the chemical irritant causes only minor effects.
summary: French police have extensively used tear gas during recent protests, causing grievous injuries. Thousands of women report acutely painful periods and increased bleeding, challenging the belief that tear gas has only minor effects.
author: France 24

title: Pope Leo XIV Urges Men to Respect Wives Amid Latin American Femicide Crisis
content: Pope Leo XIV concluded the first leg of his 12‑day Latin American tour by urging men to respect their wives. He highlighted that the region has recorded nearly 20,000 female homicide victims in the past five years, most of whom were killed by a current or former partner.
summary: Pope Leo XIV urged men to respect their wives as he wrapped up the first leg of his 12‑day tour of Latin America. The region recorded nearly 20,000 instances of women being killed over the past five years alone, most of them murdered by a current or former partner.
author: France 24

title: France says Europe will join US‑mediated Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi
content: France’s foreign minister, Jean‑Noël Barrot, announced on Sunday that France will join the upcoming Abu Dhabi peace summit aimed at ending the Ukraine war, and that European nations will be represented at the event. The talks are scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday and will be mediated by the United States.
summary: France will participate in the upcoming Abu Dhabi peace talks on ending the Ukraine war, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Sunday. Europeans will be represented at the summit, which will be held under US mediation on Tuesday and Wednesday.
author: France 24

title: Poland launches terrorism probe after shooting kills six, injures 16
content:
Poland has launched a terrorism investigation after a deadly shooting that killed six people and injured 16.

A 24‑year‑old Polish suspect, reportedly fascinated by far‑right ideologies, is under investigation for a possible extremist motive. Krakow's main square remains sealed, and two days of national mourning have been declared for the victims.
summary: Poland opened a terrorism investigation after a shooting left six dead and 16 injured. A 24‑year‑old Polish suspect, reportedly fascinated by far‑right ideologies, is being investigated, Krakow’s main square remains sealed, and two days of national mourning were declared.
author: France 24

title: Migrant boat sinks off Senegal, at least 34 dead
content: A migrant vessel traveling the hazardous Atlantic Ocean route from West Africa to Europe sank off Senegal’s coast, authorities said Sunday. The incident killed at least 34 people. Only one survivor has been located, and an indeterminate number of passengers remain missing.
summary: A boat carrying migrants on the hazardous Atlantic Ocean route from West Africa to Europe sank off the coast of Senegal, killing at least 34 people, authorities said Sunday. Only one survivor has been found and an indeterminate number of people remain missing.
author: France 24

title: Eisenkot tasked by Herzog to form coalition government
content: Israel’s former military chief Gadi Eisenkot was appointed by President Isaac Herzog to attempt to form a government. Lacking a clear parliamentary majority, Eisenkot faces an uphill task building a coalition with Israel’s fragmented minor parties.
summary: Israel's ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot was tapped by President Isaac Herzog to form a government. His lack of a clear majority in parliament makes coalition-building with divided minor parties an uphill struggle.
author: France 24

title: Pope Leo heads to Argentina for second leg of South America tour after Uruguay
content:
Pope Leo is set to continue his South American tour by heading to Argentina for the second leg, where he is expected to attract the largest crowd of his papacy to date. The pontiff has already concluded his initial visit to Uruguay.

title: Polish prosecutors launch terrorism probe into Kraków market shooting
content:
Polish prosecutors have opened a terrorism investigation following a shooting in Kraków’s market square that killed six people, including a Briton, and injured 17. The 24‑year‑old gunman opened fire on Saturday afternoon, and authorities say the attack was probably inspired by far‑right ideologies.

Police confirmed on Sunday that three people were found dead at the gunman’s home: his father, 53, his mother, 52, and his sister, 21. The deaths were discovered after the Saturday attack.

title: UK spent £100m on unused Brexit border inspection posts, five of seven never operational
content:
The National Audit Office has revealed that the United Kingdom wasted at least £100 million of taxpayers’ money on border inspection posts that never entered service. Five of the seven facilities built in England and Wales never reached an operational stage, a result of the Conservative Party’s indecision over how to check goods after Brexit.

The audit’s broader estimate places the total cost of Brexit at about £4.7 billion. That figure includes the years‑long transformation of software used for customs declarations and other systems developed to support the UK’s exit from the single market.
summary: The UK wasted at least £100m of taxpayers’ money on “zombie” Brexit border inspection posts that were never used. Five of the seven facilities in England and Wales never reached an operational stage as Tories vacillated over plans to check goods.
