title: Cyber‑attack heats European supermarket freezers, causing food loss worth millions
content: Acts of greyzone aggression aim to spread panic. Europe has to show the saboteurs that we are resilient It was as though a ghostly hand had switched the settings on supermarket freezers across Europe from “freeze” to “defrost”. From Finland to Ireland, they suddenly began heating up, many reaching 50C and food worth millions of euros had to be thrown away. But no actual hand was needed to cause the meltdown. This was a cyber-attack, or rather a chain of attacks. Like pretty much everything else in 2026, supermarket freezers are digitally enabled. That makes them smarter and more efficient, but like everything else that is connected to the internet, it also makes them more vulnerable. Russian hacktivists claimed they were behind some of the supermarket sabotage, but no one knows for sure. It could also be Iran, Iranian proxies, North Korea – or unaffiliated bedroom hackers. When Transport for London suffered a devastating hack two years ago, the culprits turned out to be two British teenagers. Governments regularly warn retailers and other companies about cyber-attacks and even provide cyber-defence training to businesses. The lessons of costly ransomware and cyber-attacks also mean many big organisations and retailers have become much better at keeping their payments and logistics systems safe. Elisabeth Braw is a Swedish security expert and the author of The Undersea War : The International Battle for Supremacy at the Bottom of the World
summary: A cyber‑attack switched supermarket freezers from “freeze” to “defrost” across Europe, raising temperatures to about 50 °C and forcing the disposal of food worth millions of euros. Russian hacktivists claimed responsibility, though Iran, North Korea or unaffiliated hackers are also possible, and a similar hack previously hit Transport for London by two British teenagers.

summary: Three weeks after lung cancer surgery, Pope Francis began a three‑nation Latin American tour, saying he felt better than he looked. On his first stop in Uruguay, he urged healthcare for all.
author: France 24

title: US urges China to honor Busan trade deal commitments on agriculture and rare earths
content: The United States urged Beijing to honor the commitments outlined in a 2025 trade accord, emphasizing the need for China to fulfill obligations related to agricultural purchases and the supply of rare earths. China responded by voicing concern over what it described as the United States’ “economic, trade restrictive” measures.
summary: The United States urged Beijing to meet commitments from a 2025 Busan accord, specifically on agricultural purchases and rare‑earth supply. China expressed concern over the United States' "economic, trade restrictive" measures.

title: France to spend extra €4 bn on education amid protests and rising debt costs
content: France intends to allocate an additional €4 billion to education while the country experiences nationwide protests. At the same time, public debt is rising and the cost of servicing that debt is increasing, prompting questions about the government’s remaining fiscal flexibility.
summary: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. Public debt is mounting and interest costs are climbing, limiting fiscal room.

title: Russia airstrikes hit Kyiv bridge and energy facilities before Abu Dhabi talks
content: Russia carried out airstrikes on Kyiv, striking a major bridge and energy facilities in the Kyiv region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Moscow was attempting to push Ukraine into a blackout ahead of upcoming trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi.
summary: The strikes hit a major bridge and energy facilities in the Kyiv region. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Moscow of trying to “push” Ukraine “into a blackout” ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi.

title: Probation warns early‑release prisoners may become homeless as temporary housing ends
content:
Charities say the case of a 37‑year‑old man named James highlights a “fatal flaw” in the plan announced by Andy Burnham to end rough sleeping in England by Christmas. James was released from prison in August and placed in temporary probation accommodation in Somerset, which is set to end in four days, leaving him with no housing options.

He told reporters that he has contacted MPs, solicitors, probation and the council but received no help, and he is considering asking to be recalled to prison as November’s cold weather approaches. Probation staff have warned that early‑release prisoners like James are at risk of street homelessness.
summary: Charities say the situation exposes a fatal flaw in Andy Burnham’s plan to end rough sleeping in England by Christmas. A 37‑year‑old man released in August faces street homelessness in four days after his temporary probation accommodation in Somerset expires, prompting him to consider returning to prison.

title: TikTok used by OnlyFans performers to covertly market sex industry to girls
content: Researchers say popular performers covertly market OnlyFans content and tell followers about wealthy lifestyle TikTok is helping to promote and normalise the sex industry, allowing “sexfluencers” to post videos aimed at marketing pornographic content they have uploaded elsewhere on sites such as OnlyFans, a report indicates. After studying non-explicit content posted on TikTok over the course of a year by some of OnlyFans’ most popular young female performers, researchers said the women buried coded references to pornography in “girly lifestyle content” that showed them shopping, playing with their pets, baking or offering skincare advice.
summary: TikTok used by OnlyFans performers to covertly market sex industry to girls.
